1	// andesim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andesim [<cmd>] [--mode M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// `run` is the default command: when the first token is not a known
9	// subcommand (and not a top-level help flag), the whole line parses as
10	// `run ...`, so `andesim --mode fast prog.elf` works without typing `run`.
11	//
12	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
13	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
14	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
15	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
16	#ifndef ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
17	#define ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
18	
19	#include <string>
20	#include <string_view>
21	#include <vector>
22	
23	namespace andes_sim {
24	
25	// True for the known command names (run/list/doctor/profile). The single
26	// source of truth shared by the parser (default-command rule) and main's
27	// dispatch.
28	bool is_subcommand(std::string_view name);
29	
30	struct Cli {
31	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
32	  std::string model;                      // --mode fast|cycle|hybrid (field stays 'model': the concept, see list models)
33	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
34	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc
35	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
36	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the sizes stay strings here and are
37	  // parsed where they are used.
38	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
39	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
40	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
41	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
42	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
43	  std::string log_level;                  // --log-level 0..6 (vsim scale; "" => info)
44	  std::string log_file;                   // --log-file <path> (full trace capture)
45	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
46	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
47	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
48	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
49	  bool print_memmap = false;              // --print-memmap (run --mode hybrid)
50	  bool verify = false;                    // --verify (run --mode hybrid)
51	  bool gdb = false;                       // --gdb (fast: QEMU gdbstub; cycle: vsim JTAG + ICEman)
52	  std::string gdb_port;                   // --gdb-port (fast: default 1234; cycle: default 9104)
53	  // profile's report knobs (values stay strings; cmd_profile applies the
54	  // defaults where they are used, like mem_size/gdb_port above).
55	  std::string limit;                      // --limit (profile; "" => 50)
56	  std::string min_iters;                  // --min-iters (profile; "" => 1)
57	  std::string addr2line;                  // --addr2line (profile; "" => auto)
58	  bool raw = false;                       // --raw (profile: dump the plugin log)
59	  bool llm = true;                        // --llm / --no-llm (profile report format)
60	  bool optimize_rvv = true;               // --optimize-rvv / --no-optimize-rvv (profile)
61	  bool no_source = false;                 // --no-source (profile: skip addr2line)
62	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
63	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
64	};

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# `andesim profile` contract: hot inner-loop detection rides the engine's own
3	# QEMU config. Like hybrid, profile picks a cycle-accurate engine (--engine or
4	# the sole one) and derives the QEMU launch from it: -cpu from the engine's
5	# `--print-qemu-config` driver globals, vlen from its --describe, the staged
6	# qemu.cfg as -readconfig. Layers:
7	#
8	#   1. unit (fast, pure): the profile core (parse/filter/nest/render/argv)
9	#      plus the CLI parse of the profile flags.
10	#   2. fake engines (no real vsim, no QEMU): throwaway engine scripts that
11	#      answer --describe AND --print-qemu-config drive the real
12	#      discover -> resolve -> probe -> argv path; --dry-run prints the exact
13	#      QEMU command without spawning it, so every assertion is deterministic.
14	#   3. real engine (guarded): the probe/argv against a built sim_* binary,
15	#      still --dry-run (the full QEMU run is covered by
16	#      tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotIterationLoop_measure.sh).
17	set -uo pipefail
18	
19	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
20	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
21	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
22	
23	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
24	
25	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
26	
27	# 1. unit: profile core + CLI parse
28	"$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-profile-test" || fail "profile unit tests failed"
29	"$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-cli-test" || fail "cli unit tests failed"
30	
31	# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
32	TMP=$(mktemp -d)
33	trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
34	
35	# mkengine DIR FILE ID VLEN CPU: a fake cycle-accurate engine whose
36	# --print-qemu-config names CPU (a minimal but valid -readconfig text). An
37	# empty CPU makes the probe FAIL (exit 1), like an engine without the hook.
38	mkengine() {
39	  local f="$1/$2"
40	  cat >"$f" <<EOF
41	#!/bin/sh
42	if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
43	  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","xlen":64,"vlen":$4,"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
44	elif [ "\$1" = "--print-qemu-config" ]; then
45	  [ -n "$5" ] || exit 1
46	  printf '[global]\ndriver = "$5-riscv-cpu"\nproperty = "vlen"\nvalue = "$4"\n'
47	else
48	  echo "RAN:\$*"
49	fi
50	EOF
51	  chmod +x "$f"
52	}
53	
54	D1="$TMP/one"; D2="$TMP/two"; DE="$TMP/empty"; DN="$TMP/nocfg"
55	mkdir -p "$D1" "$D2" "$DE" "$DN"
56	mkengine "$D1" v1 "vsim:v1" 256 "andes-ax45mpv"
57	mkengine "$D2" v1 "vsim:v1" 512 "andes-ax45mpv"
58	mkengine "$D2" v2 "vsim:v2" 128 "andes-ax66"
59	mkengine "$DN" v1 "vsim:v1" 512 ""   # probe fails -> default -cpu, no -readconfig
60	
61	DUMMY="$TMP/dummy.elf"; : >"$DUMMY"
62	
63	# 2a. sole engine is the default; the dry-run shows the full QEMU command with
64	# the engine-derived -cpu (model from the probe, vlen from --describe), the
65	# staged -readconfig, the plugin with default limit/min_iters, and -bios.
66	expect 0 '\-plugin .*libhotIterationLoop\.so,limit=50,min_iters=1' \
67	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
68	expect 0 '\-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=256' \
69	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
70	expect 0 '\-readconfig .*/qemu\.cfg' \
71	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
72	expect 0 '\-bios .*dummy\.elf' \
73	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
74	expect 0 'dry-run: 1 command\(s\), not executed' \
75	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
76	# 2b. --limit/--min-iters ride the -plugin arg; --mem-size becomes -m; the
77	# post--- args land on the QEMU command verbatim.
78	expect 0 '\-plugin .*,limit=7,min_iters=3' \
79	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --limit 7 --min-iters 3 "$DUMMY"
80	expect 0 '\-m 256M' \
81	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --mem-size 256M "$DUMMY"
82	expect 0 '\-icount shift=0' \
83	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY" -- -icount shift=0
84	# 2c. two engines, no --engine: ambiguous, names both; --engine picks one and
85	# its OWN cpu/vlen pair follows (ax66 + vlen=128).
86	expect 2 'multiple cycle-accurate.*vsim:v1.*vsim:v2' \
87	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
88	expect 0 '\-cpu andes-ax66,vlen=128' \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# `andesim profile` contract: hot inner-loop detection rides the engine's own
# QEMU config. Like hybrid, profile picks a cycle-accurate engine (--engine or
# the sole one) and derives the QEMU launch from it: -cpu from the engine's
# `--print-qemu-config` driver globals, vlen from its --describe, the staged
# qemu.cfg as -readconfig. Layers:
#
#   1. unit (fast, pure): the profile core (parse/filter/nest/render/argv)
#      plus the CLI parse of the profile flags.
#   2. fake engines (no real vsim, no QEMU): throwaway engine scripts that
#      answer --describe AND --print-qemu-config drive the real
#      discover -> resolve -> probe -> argv path; --dry-run prints the exact
#      QEMU command without spawning it, so every assertion is deterministic.
#   3. real engine (guarded): the probe/argv against a built sim_* binary,
#      still --dry-run (the full QEMU run is covered by
#      tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotIterationLoop_measure.sh).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: profile core + CLI parse
"$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-profile-test" || fail "profile unit tests failed"
"$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-cli-test" || fail "cli unit tests failed"

# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# mkengine DIR FILE ID VLEN CPU: a fake cycle-accurate engine whose
# --print-qemu-config names CPU (a minimal but valid -readconfig text). An
# empty CPU makes the probe FAIL (exit 1), like an engine without the hook.
mkengine() {
  local f="$1/$2"
  cat >"$f" <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","xlen":64,"vlen":$4,"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
elif [ "\$1" = "--print-qemu-config" ]; then
  [ -n "$5" ] || exit 1
  printf '[global]\ndriver = "$5-riscv-cpu"\nproperty = "vlen"\nvalue = "$4"\n'
else
  echo "RAN:\$*"
fi
EOF
  chmod +x "$f"
}

D1="$TMP/one"; D2="$TMP/two"; DE="$TMP/empty"; DN="$TMP/nocfg"
mkdir -p "$D1" "$D2" "$DE" "$DN"
mkengine "$D1" v1 "vsim:v1" 256 "andes-ax45mpv"
mkengine "$D2" v1 "vsim:v1" 512 "andes-ax45mpv"
mkengine "$D2" v2 "vsim:v2" 128 "andes-ax66"
mkengine "$DN" v1 "vsim:v1" 512 ""   # probe fails -> default -cpu, no -readconfig

DUMMY="$TMP/dummy.elf"; : >"$DUMMY"

# 2a. sole engine is the default; the dry-run shows the full QEMU command with
# the engine-derived -cpu (model from the probe, vlen from --describe), the
# staged -readconfig, the plugin with default limit/min_iters, and -bios.
expect 0 '\-plugin .*libhotIterationLoop\.so,limit=50,min_iters=1' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
expect 0 '\-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=256' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
expect 0 '\-readconfig .*/qemu\.cfg' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
expect 0 '\-bios .*dummy\.elf' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
expect 0 'dry-run: 1 command\(s\), not executed' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
# 2b. --limit/--min-iters ride the -plugin arg; --mem-size becomes -m; the
# post--- args land on the QEMU command verbatim.
expect 0 '\-plugin .*,limit=7,min_iters=3' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --limit 7 --min-iters 3 "$DUMMY"
expect 0 '\-m 256M' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --mem-size 256M "$DUMMY"
expect 0 '\-icount shift=0' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY" -- -icount shift=0
# 2c. two engines, no --engine: ambiguous, names both; --engine picks one and
# its OWN cpu/vlen pair follows (ax66 + vlen=128).
expect 2 'multiple cycle-accurate.*vsim:v1.*vsim:v2' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
expect 0 '\-cpu andes-ax66,vlen=128' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --engine vsim:v2 "$DUMMY"
# 2d. no cycle-accurate engine discoverable: the same clear error hybrid gives
expect 2 'no cycle-accurate engine' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
expect 2 "no engine 'vsim:nope'" \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --engine vsim:nope "$DUMMY"
# 2e. an engine whose --print-qemu-config fails: tolerant fallback -- default
# -cpu family, vlen still synced from --describe, and NO -readconfig.
out=$(env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DN" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --log-level 3 "$DUMMY" 2>&1 </dev/null)
rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "probe-less engine: rc=$rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq -- '-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512' \
  || fail "probe-less engine: missing default -cpu: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-readconfig' \
  && fail "probe-less engine: unexpected -readconfig: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'no --print-qemu-config' \
  || fail "probe-less engine: missing the fallback warning: $out"
# 2f. CLI shape errors
expect 2 'missing ELF' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run
expect 2 'QEMU args go after --' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'ELF not found' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$TMP/nope.elf"
# 2g. run-only flags are rejected loudly, not silently ignored
expect 2 'not a profile option' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --trigger marker "$DUMMY"
expect 2 'not a profile option' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --mode fast "$DUMMY"
expect 2 'not a profile option' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --verify "$DUMMY"
# 2h. profile appears in the help tree
expect 0 'profile' "$BIN" --help
expect 0 'profile' "$BIN" profile --help
echo "[ok] fake-engine profile: engine-derived cfg, errors, dry-run argv"

# 3. real engine (guarded, still --dry-run): the staged cfg + cpu come from the
# actual sim_ax45mpv_premium probe.
SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
if [ -x "$SIM" ]; then
  expect 0 '\-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=[0-9]+' \
    "$BIN" profile --dry-run --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
  expect 0 '\-readconfig .*/qemu\.cfg' \
    "$BIN" profile --dry-run --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
  echo "[ok] real engine probe: -cpu/-readconfig derived from sim_ax45mpv_premium"
else
  echo "[skip] real engine layer: no built $SIM"
fi

ok "profile: engine-synced QEMU profile command"

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env ("" when neither is set).
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR
}

## Solid findings

**1. `driver/cmd_profile.cpp` 449-464 — the two `LoopSyms`-building branches duplicate the same loop.**
Both the `if (cli.llm)` and `else` arms build `std::vector<LoopSyms> syms` by iterating and calling `make_syms(elf, X.start, X.end, src_map)` — the llm arm over `loops`, the table arm over `rows`. `build_loops` copies `rows[i].start/end` straight into `loops[i]` in the same order, and `rows` is already truncated to `limit` by `filter_loops` (so `loops.size() == rows.size()`), which means the two `syms` vectors are element-for-element identical.
- Maintenance cost: the syms-construction loop (reserve + push_back + `make_syms` call) is written twice; any change to how a loop is symbolized must be edited in two places.
- Simpler form: build `syms` once from `rows` before the branch, then `if (cli.llm) { auto loops = build_loops(rows, limit); report = render_llm(loops, syms, ...); } else { report = render_table(rows, syms, ...); }`. `syms` is parallel to both `rows` and `loops`, so both renderers accept it unchanged. Output identical.

**2. `driver/profile.cpp` 231-233 and 377-379 — the `src_short` lambda is a redundant wrapper around `src_basename`, defined twice.**
`src_short(full) = full.empty() ? "" : src_basename(full)`, but `src_basename` already returns `""` for an empty argument (line 202), so `src_short(x) == src_basename(x)` for every input. The wrapper is defined identically inside both `render_llm` and `render_table`. `render_llm` even calls `src_basename` directly at 312/315/316 while routing 257 through `src_short` — inconsistent within one function.
- Maintenance cost: a no-op indirection duplicated across two functions; a reader must confirm the empty-guard isn't doing something `src_basename` doesn't.
- Simpler form: delete both lambdas, call `src_basename(...)` at the three use sites (257, 381 x2). Byte-identical report text.

**3. `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_profile.sh` 66-75 (and 129-132) — consecutive `expect` blocks re-run one identical command to check different regexes.**
`expect` runs its command once per call (`tests/lib/log.sh:17`). Lines 66-75 spawn the exact same `env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"` five times; the real-engine block 129-132 spawns its command twice. The command line is written out verbatim 5x / 2x.
- Maintenance cost: renaming the env var, the flag, or `$DUMMY` requires editing 5 (resp. 2) identical copies; the single command is not a single source of truth.
- Simpler form: capture once and grep N times — exactly the idiom block 2e (97-105) already uses in this same file (`out=$(env ... "$BIN" profile ...)`, then `grep -Eq ...`). Same assertions, one spawn. (This is a within-file inconsistency, not a call to abandon `expect` generally.)
